### Genome Parameters

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--genomeLoad`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
mode of shared memory usage for the genome files. Only used with --runMode alignReads.

- LoadAndKeep     ... load genome into shared and keep it in memory after run
- LoadAndRemove   ... load genome into shared but remove it after run
- LoadAndExit     ... load genome into shared memory and exit, keeping the genome in memory for future runs
- Remove          ... do not map anything, just remove loaded genome from memory
- NoSharedMemory  ... do not use shared memory, each job will have its own private copy of the genome
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"NoSharedMemory"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--genomeFastaFiles`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
path(s) to the fasta files with the genome sequences, separated by spaces. These files should be plain text FASTA files, they *cannot* be zipped.

Required for the genome generation (--runMode genomeGenerate). Can also be used in the mapping (--runMode alignReads) to add extra (new) sequences to the genome (e.g. spike-ins).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `file`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"genome.fasta"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--genomeFileSizes`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
genome files exact sizes in bytes. Typically, this should not be defined by the user.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--genomeTransformOutput`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
which output to transform back to original genome

- SAM     ... SAM/BAM alignments
- SJ      ... splice junctions (SJ.out.tab)
- None    ... no transformation of the output
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--genomeChrSetMitochondrial`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
names of the mitochondrial chromosomes. Presently only used for STARsolo statistics output/
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"chrM"`, `"M"`, `"MT"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::

:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readFilesType`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
format of input read files

- Fastx       ... FASTA or FASTQ
- SAM SE      ... SAM or BAM single-end reads; for BAM use --readFilesCommand samtools view
- SAM PE      ... SAM or BAM paired-end reads; for BAM use --readFilesCommand samtools view
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Fastx"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readFilesSAMattrKeep`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
for --readFilesType SAM SE/PE, which SAM tags to keep in the output BAM, e.g.: --readFilesSAMtagsKeep RG PL

- All     ... keep all tags
- None    ... do not keep any tags
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"All"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readFilesManifest`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
path to the "manifest" file with the names of read files. The manifest file should contain 3 tab-separated columns:

paired-end reads: read1_file_name $tab$ read2_file_name $tab$ read_group_line.
single-end reads: read1_file_name $tab$ -               $tab$ read_group_line.
Spaces, but not tabs are allowed in file names.
If read_group_line does not start with ID:, it can only contain one ID field, and ID: will be added to it.
If read_group_line starts with ID:, it can contain several fields separated by $tab$, and all fields will be be copied verbatim into SAM @RG header line.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`file`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"manifest.txt"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readFilesPrefix`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
prefix for the read files names, i.e. it will be added in front of the strings in --readFilesIn
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readFilesCommand`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
command line to execute for each of the input file. This command should generate FASTA or FASTQ text and send it to stdout

For example: zcat - to uncompress .gz files, bzcat - to uncompress .bz2 files, etc.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readMapNumber`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
number of reads to map from the beginning of the file

-1: map all reads
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `-1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readMatesLengthsIn`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Equal/NotEqual - lengths of names,sequences,qualities for both mates are the same  / not the same. NotEqual is safe in all situations.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"NotEqual"`

::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--readNameSeparator`
:::

character(s) separating the part of the read names that will be trimmed in output (read name after space is always trimmed)

### Read Clipping

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--clipAdapterType`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
adapter clipping type

- Hamming ... adapter clipping based on Hamming distance, with the number of mismatches controlled by --clip5pAdapterMMp
- CellRanger4 ... 5p and 3p adapter clipping similar to CellRanger4. Utilizes Opal package by Martin Sosic: https://github.com/Martinsos/opal
- None ... no adapter clipping, all other clip* parameters are disregarded
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Hamming"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--clip3pNbases`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
number(s) of bases to clip from 3p of each mate. If one value is given, it will be assumed the same for both mates.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--clip3pAdapterSeq`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
adapter sequences to clip from 3p of each mate.  If one value is given, it will be assumed the same for both mates.

- polyA ... polyA sequence with the length equal to read length
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--clip3pAdapterMMp`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max proportion of mismatches for 3p adapter clipping for each mate.  If one value is given, it will be assumed the same for both mates.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `double`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0.1`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--clip3pAfterAdapterNbases`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
number of bases to clip from 3p of each mate after the adapter clipping. If one value is given, it will be assumed the same for both mates.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--clip5pNbases`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
number(s) of bases to clip from 5p of each mate. If one value is given, it will be assumed the same for both mates.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::::

::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outTmpKeep`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
whether to keep the temporary files after STAR runs is finished

- None ... remove all temporary files
- All ... keep all files
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outStd`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
which output will be directed to stdout (standard out)

- Log                    ... log messages
- SAM                    ... alignments in SAM format (which normally are output to Aligned.out.sam file), normal standard output will go into Log.std.out
- BAM_Unsorted           ... alignments in BAM format, unsorted. Requires --outSAMtype BAM Unsorted
- BAM_SortedByCoordinate ... alignments in BAM format, sorted by coordinate. Requires --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate
- BAM_Quant              ... alignments to transcriptome in BAM format, unsorted. Requires --quantMode TranscriptomeSAM
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Log"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outReadsUnmapped`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
output of unmapped and partially mapped (i.e. mapped only one mate of a paired end read) reads in separate file(s).

- None    ... no output
- Fastx   ... output in separate fasta/fastq files, Unmapped.out.mate1/2
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outQSconversionAdd`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
add this number to the quality score (e.g. to convert from Illumina to Sanger, use -31)
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outMultimapperOrder`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
order of multimapping alignments in the output files

- Old_2.4             ... quasi-random order used before 2.5.0
- Random              ... random order of alignments for each multi-mapper. Read mates (pairs) are always adjacent, all alignment for each read stay together. This option will become default in the future releases.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Old_2.4"`

`--outSAMtype`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
type of SAM/BAM output

1st word:

- BAM  ... output BAM without sorting
- SAM  ... output SAM without sorting
- None ... no SAM/BAM output

2nd, 3rd:

- Unsorted           ... standard unsorted
- SortedByCoordinate ... sorted by coordinate. This option will allocate extra memory for sorting which can be specified by --limitBAMsortRAM.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"SAM"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMmode`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
mode of SAM output

- None ... no SAM output
- Full ... full SAM output
- NoQS ... full SAM but without quality scores
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Full"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMstrandField`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Cufflinks-like strand field flag

- None        ... not used
- intronMotif ... strand derived from the intron motif. This option changes the output alignments: reads with inconsistent and/or non-canonical introns are filtered out.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMattributes`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
a string of desired SAM attributes, in the order desired for the output SAM. Tags can be listed in any combination/order.

***Presets:

- None        ... no attributes
- Standard    ... NH HI AS nM
- All         ... NH HI AS nM NM MD jM jI MC ch

***Alignment:

- NH          ... number of loci the reads maps to: =1 for unique mappers, >1 for multimappers. Standard SAM tag.
- HI          ... multiple alignment index, starts with --outSAMattrIHstart (=1 by default). Standard SAM tag.
- AS          ... local alignment score, +1/-1 for matches/mismateches, score* penalties for indels and gaps. For PE reads, total score for two mates. Stadnard SAM tag.
- nM          ... number of mismatches. For PE reads, sum over two mates.
- NM          ... edit distance to the reference (number of mismatched + inserted + deleted bases) for each mate. Standard SAM tag.
- MD          ... string encoding mismatched and deleted reference bases (see standard SAM specifications). Standard SAM tag.
- jM          ... intron motifs for all junctions (i.e. N in CIGAR): 0: non-canonical; 1: GT/AG, 2: CT/AC, 3: GC/AG, 4: CT/GC, 5: AT/AC, 6: GT/AT. If splice junctions database is used, and a junction is annotated, 20 is added to its motif value.
- jI          ... start and end of introns for all junctions (1-based).
- XS          ... alignment strand according to --outSAMstrandField.
- MC          ... mate's CIGAR string. Standard SAM tag.
- ch          ... marks all segment of all chimeric alingments for --chimOutType WithinBAM output.
- cN          ... number of bases clipped from the read ends: 5' and 3'

***Variation:

- vA          ... variant allele
- vG          ... genomic coordinate of the variant overlapped by the read.
- vW          ... 1 - alignment passes WASP filtering; 2,3,4,5,6,7 - alignment does not pass WASP filtering. Requires --waspOutputMode SAMtag.

***STARsolo:

- CR CY UR UY ... sequences and quality scores of cell barcodes and UMIs for the solo* demultiplexing.
- GX GN       ... gene ID and gene name for unique-gene reads.
- gx gn       ... gene IDs and gene names for unique- and multi-gene reads.
- CB UB       ... error-corrected cell barcodes and UMIs for solo* demultiplexing. Requires --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate.
- sM          ... assessment of CB and UMI.
- sS          ... sequence of the entire barcode (CB,UMI,adapter).
- sQ          ... quality of the entire barcode.

***Unsupported/undocumented:

- ha          ... haplotype (1/2) when mapping to the diploid genome. Requires genome generated with --genomeTransformType Diploid .
- rB          ... alignment block read/genomic coordinates.
- vR          ... read coordinate of the variant.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Standard"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMattrIHstart`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
start value for the IH attribute. 0 may be required by some downstream software, such as Cufflinks or StringTie.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMunmapped`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
output of unmapped reads in the SAM format

1st word:

- None   ... no output
- Within ... output unmapped reads within the main SAM file (i.e. Aligned.out.sam)

2nd word:

- KeepPairs ... record unmapped mate for each alignment, and, in case of unsorted output, keep it adjacent to its mapped mate. Only affects multi-mapping reads.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMorder`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
type of sorting for the SAM output

Paired: one mate after the other for all paired alignments
PairedKeepInputOrder: one mate after the other for all paired alignments, the order is kept the same as in the input FASTQ files
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Paired"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMprimaryFlag`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
which alignments are considered primary - all others will be marked with 0x100 bit in the FLAG

- OneBestScore ... only one alignment with the best score is primary
- AllBestScore ... all alignments with the best score are primary
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"OneBestScore"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMreadID`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
read ID record type

- Standard ... first word (until space) from the FASTx read ID line, removing /1,/2 from the end
- Number   ... read number (index) in the FASTx file
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Standard"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMmapqUnique`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
0 to 255: the MAPQ value for unique mappers
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `255`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMflagOR`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
0 to 65535: sam FLAG will be bitwise OR'd with this value, i.e. FLAG=FLAG | outSAMflagOR. This is applied after all flags have been set by STAR, and after outSAMflagAND. Can be used to set specific bits that are not set otherwise.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMflagAND`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
0 to 65535: sam FLAG will be bitwise AND'd with this value, i.e. FLAG=FLAG & outSAMflagOR. This is applied after all flags have been set by STAR, but before outSAMflagOR. Can be used to unset specific bits that are not set otherwise.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `65535`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMattrRGline`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
SAM/BAM read group line. The first word contains the read group identifier and must start with "ID:", e.g. --outSAMattrRGline ID:xxx CN:yy "DS:z z z".

xxx will be added as RG tag to each output alignment. Any spaces in the tag values have to be double quoted.
Comma separated RG lines correspons to different (comma separated) input files in --readFilesIn. Commas have to be surrounded by spaces, e.g.
--outSAMattrRGline ID:xxx , ID:zzz "DS:z z" , ID:yyy DS:yyyy
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMheaderHD`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
@HD (header) line of the SAM header
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMheaderPG`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
extra @PG (software) line of the SAM header (in addition to STAR)
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMheaderCommentFile`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
path to the file with @CO (comment) lines of the SAM header
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMfilter`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
filter the output into main SAM/BAM files

- KeepOnlyAddedReferences ... only keep the reads for which all alignments are to the extra reference sequences added with --genomeFastaFiles at the mapping stage.
- KeepAllAddedReferences ...  keep all alignments to the extra reference sequences added with --genomeFastaFiles at the mapping stage.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMmultNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max number of multiple alignments for a read that will be output to the SAM/BAM files. Note that if this value is not equal to -1, the top scoring alignment will be output first

- -1 ... all alignments (up to --outFilterMultimapNmax) will be output
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `-1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outSAMtlen`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
calculation method for the TLEN field in the SAM/BAM files

- 1 ... leftmost base of the (+)strand mate to rightmost base of the (-)mate. (+)sign for the (+)strand mate
- 2 ... leftmost base of any mate to rightmost base of any mate. (+)sign for the mate with the leftmost base. This is different from 1 for overlapping mates with protruding ends
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outBAMcompression`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
-1 to 10  BAM compression level, -1=default compression (6?), 0=no compression, 10=maximum compression
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--outBAMsortingThreadN`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
>=0: number of threads for BAM sorting. 0 will default to min(6,--runThreadN).
:::

`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`

`--outBAMsortingBinsN`

`integer`

### Alignments and Seeding

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}

Name

Description

Attributes

::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedSearchStartLmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
defines the search start point through the read - the read is split into pieces no longer than this value
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `50`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedSearchStartLmaxOverLread`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
seedSearchStartLmax normalized to read length (sum of mates' lengths for paired-end reads)
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1.0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedSearchLmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
defines the maximum length of the seeds, if =0 seed length is not limited
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedMultimapNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
only pieces that map fewer than this value are utilized in the stitching procedure
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `10000`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedPerReadNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max number of seeds per read
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1000`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedPerWindowNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max number of seeds per window
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `50`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedNoneLociPerWindow`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max number of one seed loci per window
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `10`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedSplitMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
min length of the seed sequences split by Ns or mate gap
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `12`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--seedMapMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
min length of seeds to be mapped
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `5`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignIntronMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum intron size, genomic gap is considered intron if its length>=alignIntronMin, otherwise it is considered Deletion
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `21`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignIntronMax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
maximum intron size, if 0, max intron size will be determined by (2^winBinNbits)*winAnchorDistNbins
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignMatesGapMax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
maximum gap between two mates, if 0, max intron gap will be determined by (2^winBinNbits)*winAnchorDistNbins
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignSJoverhangMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum overhang (i.e. block size) for spliced alignments
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `5`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignSJstitchMismatchNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
maximum number of mismatches for stitching of the splice junctions (-1: no limit).

(1) non-canonical motifs, (2) GT/AG and CT/AC motif, (3) GC/AG and CT/GC motif, (4) AT/AC and GT/AT motif.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`, `-1`, `0`, `0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignSJDBoverhangMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum overhang (i.e. block size) for annotated (sjdb) spliced alignments
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `3`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignSplicedMateMapLmin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum mapped length for a read mate that is spliced
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignSplicedMateMapLminOverLmate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
alignSplicedMateMapLmin normalized to mate length
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`double`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0.66`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignWindowsPerReadNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max number of windows per read
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `10000`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignTranscriptsPerWindowNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max number of transcripts per window
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `100`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignTranscriptsPerReadNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max number of different alignments per read to consider
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `10000`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignEndsType`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
type of read ends alignment

- Local             ... standard local alignment with soft-clipping allowed
- EndToEnd          ... force end-to-end read alignment, do not soft-clip
- Extend5pOfRead1   ... fully extend only the 5p of the read1, all other ends: local alignment
- Extend5pOfReads12 ... fully extend only the 5p of the both read1 and read2, all other ends: local alignment
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Local"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignEndsProtrude`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
allow protrusion of alignment ends, i.e. start (end) of the +strand mate downstream of the start (end) of the -strand mate

1st word: int: maximum number of protrusion bases allowed
2nd word: string:

-                     ConcordantPair ... report alignments with non-zero protrusion as concordant pairs
-                     DiscordantPair ... report alignments with non-zero protrusion as discordant pairs
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"0    ConcordantPair"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignSoftClipAtReferenceEnds`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
allow the soft-clipping of the alignments past the end of the chromosomes

- Yes ... allow
- No  ... prohibit, useful for compatibility with Cufflinks
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Yes"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--alignInsertionFlush`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
how to flush ambiguous insertion positions

- None    ... insertions are not flushed
- Right   ... insertions are flushed to the right
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::::

### Chimeric Alignments

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::

Description

Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimOutType`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
type of chimeric output

- Junctions       ... Chimeric.out.junction
- SeparateSAMold  ... output old SAM into separate Chimeric.out.sam file
- WithinBAM       ... output into main aligned BAM files (Aligned.*.bam)
- WithinBAM HardClip  ... (default) hard-clipping in the CIGAR for supplemental chimeric alignments (default if no 2nd word is present)
- WithinBAM SoftClip  ... soft-clipping in the CIGAR for supplemental chimeric alignments
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Junctions"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimSegmentMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum length of chimeric segment length, if ==0, no chimeric output
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimScoreMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum total (summed) score of the chimeric segments
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimScoreDropMax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
max drop (difference) of chimeric score (the sum of scores of all chimeric segments) from the read length
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `20`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimScoreSeparation`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum difference (separation) between the best chimeric score and the next one
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `10`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimScoreJunctionNonGTAG`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
penalty for a non-GT/AG chimeric junction
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `-1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimJunctionOverhangMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
minimum overhang for a chimeric junction
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `20`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimSegmentReadGapMax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
maximum gap in the read sequence between chimeric segments
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimFilter`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
different filters for chimeric alignments

- None ... no filtering
- banGenomicN ... Ns are not allowed in the genome sequence around the chimeric junction
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"banGenomicN"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimMainSegmentMultNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
maximum number of multi-alignments for the main chimeric segment. =1 will prohibit multimapping main segments.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `10`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimMultimapNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
maximum number of chimeric multi-alignments

- 0 ... use the old scheme for chimeric detection which only considered unique alignments
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimMultimapScoreRange`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
the score range for multi-mapping chimeras below the best chimeric score. Only works with --chimMultimapNmax > 1
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimNonchimScoreDropMin`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
to trigger chimeric detection, the drop in the best non-chimeric alignment score with respect to the read length has to be greater than this value
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `20`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--chimOutJunctionFormat`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
formatting type for the Chimeric.out.junction file

- 0 ... no comment lines/headers
- 1 ... comment lines at the end of the file: command line and Nreads: total, unique/multi-mapping
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`

### WASP parameters

::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--waspOutputMode`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
WASP allele-specific output type. This is re-implementation of the original WASP mappability filtering by Bryce van de Geijn, Graham McVicker, Yoav Gilad & Jonathan K Pritchard. Please cite the original WASP paper: Nature Methods 12, 1061-1063 (2015), https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.3582 .

- SAMtag      ... add WASP tags to the alignments that pass WASP filtering
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

### STARsolo (single cell RNA-seq) parameters

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloType`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
type of single-cell RNA-seq

- CB_UMI_Simple   ... (a.k.a. Droplet) one UMI and one Cell Barcode of fixed length in read2, e.g. Drop-seq and 10X Chromium.
- CB_UMI_Complex  ... multiple Cell Barcodes of varying length, one UMI of fixed length and one adapter sequence of fixed length are allowed in read2 only (e.g. inDrop, ddSeq).
- CB_samTagOut    ... output Cell Barcode as CR and/or CB SAm tag. No UMI counting. --readFilesIn cDNA_read1 [cDNA_read2 if paired-end] CellBarcode_read . Requires --outSAMtype BAM Unsorted [and/or SortedByCoordinate]
- SmartSeq        ... Smart-seq: each cell in a separate FASTQ (paired- or single-end), barcodes are corresponding read-groups, no UMI sequences, alignments deduplicated according to alignment start and end (after extending soft-clipped bases)
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloCBwhitelist`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
file(s) with whitelist(s) of cell barcodes. Only --soloType CB_UMI_Complex allows more than one whitelist file.

- None            ... no whitelist: all cell barcodes are allowed
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloCBstart`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
cell barcode start base
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloCBlen`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
cell barcode length
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `16`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloUMIstart`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
UMI start base
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `17`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloUMIlen`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
UMI length
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `10`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloBarcodeReadLength`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
length of the barcode read

- 1   ... equal to sum of soloCBlen+soloUMIlen
- 0   ... not defined, do not check
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloBarcodeMate`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
identifies which read mate contains the barcode (CB+UMI) sequence

- 0   ... barcode sequence is on separate read, which should always be the last file in the --readFilesIn listed
- 1   ... barcode sequence is a part of mate 1
- 2   ... barcode sequence is a part of mate 2
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `0`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloCBposition`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
position of Cell Barcode(s) on the barcode read.

Presently only works with --soloType CB_UMI_Complex, and barcodes are assumed to be on Read2.
Format for each barcode: startAnchor_startPosition_endAnchor_endPosition
start(end)Anchor defines the Anchor Base for the CB: 0: read start; 1: read end; 2: adapter start; 3: adapter end
start(end)Position is the 0-based position with of the CB start(end) with respect to the Anchor Base
String for different barcodes are separated by space.
Example: inDrop (Zilionis et al, Nat. Protocols, 2017):
--soloCBposition  0_0_2_-1  3_1_3_8
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloUMIposition`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
position of the UMI on the barcode read, same as soloCBposition

Example: inDrop (Zilionis et al, Nat. Protocols, 2017):
--soloCBposition  3_9_3_14
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloAdapterSequence`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
adapter sequence to anchor barcodes. Only one adapter sequence is allowed.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloAdapterMismatchesNmax`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
maximum number of mismatches allowed in adapter sequence.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloCBmatchWLtype`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
matching the Cell Barcodes to the WhiteList

- Exact                           ... only exact matches allowed
- 1MM                             ... only one match in whitelist with 1 mismatched base allowed. Allowed CBs have to have at least one read with exact match.
- 1MM_multi                       ... multiple matches in whitelist with 1 mismatched base allowed, posterior probability calculation is used choose one of the matches.

Allowed CBs have to have at least one read with exact match. This option matches best with CellRanger 2.2.0

- 1MM_multi_pseudocounts          ... same as 1MM_Multi, but pseudocounts of 1 are added to all whitelist barcodes.
- 1MM_multi_Nbase_pseudocounts    ... same as 1MM_multi_pseudocounts, multimatching to WL is allowed for CBs with N-bases. This option matches best with CellRanger >= 3.0.0
- EditDist_2                    ... allow up to edit distance of 3 fpr each of the barcodes. May include one deletion + one insertion. Only works with --soloType CB_UMI_Complex. Matches to multiple passlist barcdoes are not allowed. Similar to ParseBio Split-seq pipeline.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"1MM_multi"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloInputSAMattrBarcodeSeq`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
when inputting reads from a SAM file (--readsFileType SAM SE/PE), these SAM attributes mark the barcode sequence (in proper order).

For instance, for 10X CellRanger or STARsolo BAMs, use --soloInputSAMattrBarcodeSeq CR UR .
This parameter is required when running STARsolo with input from SAM.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloInputSAMattrBarcodeQual`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
when inputting reads from a SAM file (--readsFileType SAM SE/PE), these SAM attributes mark the barcode qualities (in proper order).

For instance, for 10X CellRanger or STARsolo BAMs, use --soloInputSAMattrBarcodeQual CY UY .
If this parameter is '-' (default), the quality 'H' will be assigned to all bases.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloStrand`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
strandedness of the solo libraries:

- Unstranded  ... no strand information
- Forward     ... read strand same as the original RNA molecule
- Reverse     ... read strand opposite to the original RNA molecule
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Forward"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloFeatures`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
genomic features for which the UMI counts per Cell Barcode are collected

- Gene            ... genes: reads match the gene transcript
- SJ              ... splice junctions: reported in SJ.out.tab
- GeneFull        ... full gene (pre-mRNA): count all reads overlapping genes' exons and introns
- GeneFull_ExonOverIntron ... full gene (pre-mRNA): count all reads overlapping genes' exons and introns: prioritize 100% overlap with exons
- GeneFull_Ex50pAS        ... full gene (pre-RNA): count all reads overlapping genes' exons and introns: prioritize >50% overlap with exons. Do not count reads with 100% exonic overlap in the antisense direction.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Gene"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloMultiMappers`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
counting method for reads mapping to multiple genes

- Unique     ... count only reads that map to unique genes
- Uniform    ... uniformly distribute multi-genic UMIs to all genes
- Rescue     ... distribute UMIs proportionally to unique+uniform counts (~ first iteration of EM)
- PropUnique ... distribute UMIs proportionally to unique mappers, if present, and uniformly if not.
- EM         ... multi-gene UMIs are distributed using Expectation Maximization algorithm
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Unique"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloUMIdedup`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
type of UMI deduplication (collapsing) algorithm

- 1MM_All                     ... all UMIs with 1 mismatch distance to each other are collapsed (i.e. counted once).
- 1MM_Directional_UMItools    ... follows the "directional" method from the UMI-tools by Smith, Heger and Sudbery (Genome Research 2017).
- 1MM_Directional             ... same as 1MM_Directional_UMItools, but with more stringent criteria for duplicate UMIs
- Exact                       ... only exactly matching UMIs are collapsed.
- NoDedup                     ... no deduplication of UMIs, count all reads.
- 1MM_CR                      ... CellRanger2-4 algorithm for 1MM UMI collapsing.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"1MM_All"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloUMIfiltering`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
type of UMI filtering (for reads uniquely mapping to genes)

- -                  ... basic filtering: remove UMIs with N and homopolymers (similar to CellRanger 2.2.0).
- MultiGeneUMI       ... basic + remove lower-count UMIs that map to more than one gene.
- MultiGeneUMI_All   ... basic + remove all UMIs that map to more than one gene.
- MultiGeneUMI_CR    ... basic + remove lower-count UMIs that map to more than one gene, matching CellRanger > 3.0.0 .

Only works with --soloUMIdedup 1MM_CR
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloOutFileNames`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
file names for STARsolo output:

file_name_prefix   gene_names   barcode_sequences   cell_feature_count_matrix
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Solo.out/"`, `"features.tsv"`, `"barcodes.tsv"`, `"matrix.mtx"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloCellFilter`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
cell filtering type and parameters

- None            ... do not output filtered cells
- TopCells        ... only report top cells by UMI count, followed by the exact number of cells
- CellRanger2.2   ... simple filtering of CellRanger 2.2.

Can be followed by numbers: number of expected cells, robust maximum percentile for UMI count, maximum to minimum ratio for UMI count
The harcoded values are from CellRanger: nExpectedCells=3000;  maxPercentile=0.99;  maxMinRatio=10

- EmptyDrops_CR   ... EmptyDrops filtering in CellRanger flavor. Please cite the original EmptyDrops paper: A.T.L Lun et al, Genome Biology, 20, 63 (2019): https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-019-1662-y

Can be followed by 10 numeric parameters:  nExpectedCells   maxPercentile   maxMinRatio   indMin   indMax   umiMin   umiMinFracMedian   candMaxN   FDR   simN
The harcoded values are from CellRanger:             3000            0.99            10    45000    90000      500               0.01      20000  0.01  10000
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"CellRanger2.2"`, `"3000"`, `"0.99"`, `"10"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloOutFormatFeaturesGeneField3`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
field 3 in the Gene features.tsv file. If "-", then no 3rd field is output.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Gene Expression"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--soloCellReadStats`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Output reads statistics for each CB

- Standard    ... standard output
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`
:::
::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/mapping/star_align_v273a/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/mapping/star_align_v273a);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/mapping/star_align_v273a/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
